newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Indians release hostages - report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Indians release hostages - report.

text.p: A group of Brazilian Indians released on Wednesday about 50 bus passengers they had been holding hostage since Friday, local news reports said.

The Guajajara Indians released the passengers, including many women and children, after government negotiators pledged they would respond to their demands for a new paved road and better services, SBT Television and Globo said.
A police officer in the nearby town of Grajau, in the northeastern state of Maranhao, said he could not confirm the report. Officials in Brasilia were unavailable for comment.
Residents of Grajau joined in the Indians' protest by going on strike on Monday and on Tuesday and by refusing to allows cars in and out of the town.
